sources.title: NIST DLMF §3.11(ii): Chebyshev series and Clenshaw summation
sources.review_scope: Selected E7, E9, E11 and E15 with endpoint-halving conventions; no original Clenshaw paper reading. The implementation uses full coefficients, so its final combination is derived explicitly.

sources.title: SciPy 1.14.1 BarycentricInterpolator documentation
sources.review_scope: Selected barycentric formula and interpolation-conditioning notes read during the preceding preparation. The Berrut–Trefethen paper is a bibliographic lead, not a full-text reading.

sources.title: SciPy 1.14.1 PCHIP documentation and selected source
sources.review_scope: Selected lines 202–225, 243–254, 275–298: harmonic interior derivatives, endpoint sign and 3-slope limiter, two-point case. The original Fritsch–Butland paper has not been read in full. Own formulas are independently expressed as scalar Hermite polynomials.

sources.title: SciPy 1.14.1 BSpline and CubicSpline documentation
sources.review_scope: Natural and clamped boundary conditions and the BSpline recurrence were read during preparation. No de Boor original full-text claim. SciPy is a secondary numerical companion; the rational second-derivative system is the independent reference.

sources.title: S. Mallat, A Theory for Multiresolution Signal Decomposition: The Wavelet Representation
sources.review_scope: During preparation: title/abstract, Haar example on printed p. 679, selected §III-B/C filter/downsample/inverse-pyramid and border-symmetry prose on p. 681. Extracted formula glyphs were imperfect; no complete proof or numerical-table audit is claimed.

sources.title: PyWavelets documentation: Signal extension modes
sources.review_scope: Periodic and half-sample symmetric extension and the redundancy caveat. This example defines its own append-at-each-odd-level/crop convention; it does not claim PyWavelets coefficient-layout equivalence or require PyWavelets.

implementation: independently written; no third-party source body copied
